evals.prompt: Run a live CRO audit of https://example.com — it's a SaaS landing page we send Google Ads traffic to, and the goal is free-trial signups. Test it properly in a browser.
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing-context.md first. Should drive a live browser via browsing-with-playwright: navigate to the URL, take a full-page desktop screenshot, capture the DOM/accessibility snapshot, and re-test at a mobile viewport (390px). Should run DOM measurements (above-the-fold CTA, contrast, tap targets, page performance/Web Vitals, form fields, trust signals). Should score all 7 dimensions per scoring-criteria.md and compute a weighted score out of 100 with a grade. Should do a hero-section breakdown including the 5-second test, and check message match between the Google Ads promise and the hero. Output should include an Executive summary, the Biggest constraint, a score card, Quick Wins, High-Impact Changes, Test Ideas, and 2-3 Copy Alternatives for headline and CTA. Findings should cite evidence (screenshot or DOM value).
assertions: Checks for product-marketing-context.md
Uses browsing-with-playwright to open the live URL
Captures a full-page desktop screenshot
Re-tests at a mobile viewport (resize ~390px)
Measures above-the-fold CTA visibility via the DOM
Scores all 7 dimensions and computes a weighted score with grade
Performs a hero-section breakdown with the 5-second test
Notes message match between Google Ads and the hero
Output has a score card
Output has Quick Wins, High-Impact Changes, and Test Ideas sections
Provides 2-3 headline or CTA copy alternatives
Findings cite evidence from the live page

evals.prompt: Audit https://example.com/signup for conversions and actually walk the form. Test data is fine, just don't complete any payment.
evals.expected_output: Should open the page in a live browser, snapshot to get field refs, and walk the signup form: count fields (recipe 6), fill with obvious test data, observe inline validation and the post-submit state, and screenshot each step. Should stop before any irreversible or payment action. Should defer form/flow specifics to form-cro and signup-flow-cro. Should score Friction & Flow with the field-cost rule (3 baseline, 7+ heavy drop) and report required fields, input types (mobile keyboard), and autofill. Output follows the report template.
assertions: Opens the page in a live browser
Snapshots to obtain form field refs
Counts form fields via the DOM
Fills the form with test data and observes validation
Stops before payment / irreversible actions
References form-cro and/or signup-flow-cro
Scores Friction & Flow with the field-cost rule
Reports input types and autofill for mobile

evals.prompt: QA our whole funnel for conversions: the landing page, the pricing page, and the trial signup. Links: https://example.com, https://example.com/pricing, https://example.com/trial
evals.expected_output: Should treat this as a multi-page audit: run the live-capture pass on each of the three pages (desktop + mobile screenshots, DOM measurements), and explicitly check message-match consistency across the funnel (does pricing/trial keep the landing-page promise?). Should score each page and call out the weakest step. Should apply the pricing-page calibration (recommended tier, anchoring) and walk the trial signup form. Output is a consolidated report with per-page findings and a prioritized action plan.
assertions: Audits all three pages live (not just the first)
Captures desktop and mobile screenshots per page
Checks message-match consistency across the funnel
Identifies the weakest funnel step
Applies pricing-page-specific calibration
Walks the trial signup form
Produces a consolidated prioritized action plan

evals.prompt: Is my hero section any good? https://example.com — be specific about mobile.
evals.expected_output: Should open the page, screenshot the hero full-page on desktop AND mobile (390px), and evaluate the hero against hero-breakdown.md: the 7 components (eyebrow, headline, subheadline, primary CTA, secondary CTA, visual, trust strip), the 5-second test, and the spec sheet. Should confirm whether H1 + subheadline + primary CTA are above the fold on both viewports using DOM measurement, check tap-target sizes and body font on mobile, and flag conversion-killers (autoplay-with-sound, carousels). Should give 2-3 headline alternatives and concrete fixes.
assertions: Captures hero screenshots on desktop and mobile
Evaluates the 7 hero components
Performs the 5-second test
Confirms above-the-fold H1/sub/CTA via the DOM on both viewports
Checks mobile tap targets and body font size
Flags autoplay-with-sound or carousels if present
Provides 2-3 headline alternatives

evals.prompt: Can you CRO-audit our landing page? The browser won't be able to reach it — it's behind our VPN. I can paste the HTML.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize the live browser cannot reach the target and degrade gracefully: state the limitation, accept pasted HTML (or a user screenshot), and run the page-cro analysis framework over it while clearly flagging which dimensions are assumption-based rather than observed. Should still produce the structured report, and note in Limitations that performance, mobile rendering, and JS-rendered content could not be measured live.
assertions: Recognizes the live browser cannot reach the target
Degrades gracefully and states the limitation
Works from pasted HTML or a screenshot
Flags which dimensions are assumption-based
Still produces the structured report
Notes measurement limits in the Limitations section
